name: LongCat-2.5
description: LongCat-2.5 is Meituan's native multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model for long-horizon agentic tasks, with about 1.6T total parameters and roughly 48B activated per token. It builds on LongCat-2.0 with stronger native visual understanding and agentic coding, representing images as multi-level discrete tokens (RVQ over native-resolution features) so the backbone processes visual and text inputs in one token format. Training adds more long-horizon trajectories, large-scale asynchronous agentic RL across mixed harnesses, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation. Meituan also reports optimizing long-context training and W4A4 inference for domestic AI accelerators. The LongCat API (OpenAI, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic compatible) exposes it as LongCat-2.5 with a 1M-token context window; Meituan's Quick Start and FAQ list a 128K maximum output, while the Model Parameters page allows max_tokens up to 262,144. Launch pricing is a limited-time discount of $0.30 / $1.20 per MTok (cached input $0.006). Weights were not public at announcement.

benchmarks.name: BrowseComp
benchmarks.description: BrowseComp is a benchmark comprising 1,266 questions that challenge AI agents to persistently navigate the internet in search of hard-to-find, entangled information. The benchmark measures agents' ability to exercise persistence in information gathering, demonstrate creativity in web navigation, and find concise, verifiable answers. Despite the difficulty of the questions, BrowseComp is simple and easy-to-use, as predicted answers are short and easily verifiable against reference answers.

benchmarks.name: Video-MME
benchmarks.description: Video-MME is the first-ever comprehensive evaluation benchmark of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in video analysis. It features 900 videos totaling 254 hours with 2,700 human-annotated question-answer pairs across 6 primary visual domains (Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Life Record, Multilingual, and others) and 30 subfields. The benchmark evaluates models across diverse temporal dimensions (11 seconds to 1 hour), integrates multi-modal inputs including video frames, subtitles, and audio, and uses rigorous manual labeling by expert annotators for precise assessment.
